doc.code:
The task instruction.

Example:
    task = get_task_language()
    print(task)

step.description: State record (a result's state_step): 0 = initial, -1 = latest (default)

doc.tool: A state with agentview (global layout) and wrist (close range) 1024x1024 images: the current one, or the earlier state record `step` (0 = initial). Pixel (row, col) in these images feed back_project with the same step.

step.description: State record (a result's state_step): 0 = initial, -1 = latest (default)

doc.tool: Camera calibration (intrinsic K, cam-to-world extrinsic, depth range) for the current step, or for the state record `step` (high resolution).

doc.code:
Proprioception, no images: eef_pos [x, y, z] (m, world), eef_quat_xyzw, yaw (rad about world +z), gripper_width (about 0.08 open, 0.01-0.05 holding, below 0.01 closed on nothing), gripper_cmd (-1 open / +1 close, the last command), terminated (LIBERO judged the task done; it stays true), truncated.

Example:
    st = get_state()
    if st["gripper_width"] < 0.01:
        print("closed on nothing")

The current 512x512 upright camera images with calibration: agentview and wrist, each {rgb uint8[512,512,3], depth float32[512,512] metres (0 = none), intrinsic_K 3x3, extrinsic_cam2world 4x4}, plus the get_state fields. Pixel (row, col) back-projects as x = (col - cx) z / fx, y = (row - cy) z / fy in the camera frame, then extrinsic_cam2world @ [x, y, z, 1]. The agentview faces the robot (its base at the image top); the wrist camera looks down between the fingers.

Example:
    obs = get_observation()
    depth = obs["agentview"]["depth"]
    K = obs["agentview"]["intrinsic_K"]

resolution.description: The image the pixel came from: high = 1024 (default), low = 256

z_min.description: Region mode: keep pixels with world z >= z_min

z_max.description: Region mode: keep pixels with world z <= z_max

step.description: State record (a result's state_step): 0 = initial, -1 = latest (default)

doc.tool: World xyz of a pixel (row, col; row 0 = top) in the current camera image, or in state record `step`'s (the state_step of the image the pixel came from), from that state's depth world map. Region mode: row_range + col_range (+ optional z_min/z_max) returns the midpoint of world xy over that window, e.g. a container's interior center. Pixels from the 1024 images use resolution high (default).
doc.code:
World xyz {world_xyz: [x, y, z]} of pixel (row, col) of the current 512x512 image of a camera (get_observation's; row 0 = top), through its depth; an error when the pixel has no depth. Region mode: row_range + col_range (+ z_min / z_max) returns center_xyz (midpoint of world x and y over the window, median z) and median_xyz.

Example:
    p = back_project(300, 260)["world_xyz"]
    inside = back_project(row_range=[200, 260], col_range=[240, 300])["center_xyz"]

prompt.description: What to segment, e.g. 'black bowl' (or give point)

point.description: A positive point [row, col] instead of a prompt

step.description: State record (a result's state_step): 0 = initial, -1 = latest (default)

doc.tool: SAM3 segmentation of the current 1024x1024 camera image, or of state record `step`'s. Give exactly one of a text prompt or a positive point [row, col]. The top mask is projected through that state's depth world map; world_xyz is the median over mask pixels. Returns an overlay image; the reading is saved as segment_artifact.
doc.code:
SAM3 segmentation of the current 512x512 image of a camera by a text prompt (or a point [row, col]): {found, score, box [x1, y1, x2, y2], mask bool[512,512], n_pixels, centroid_rowcol [row, col], world_xyz (median over the mask's pixels with depth, or None)}.

Example:
    seg = segment("black bowl")
    if seg["found"]:
        xyz = seg["world_xyz"]

doc.tool: Whether move_to could reach a world xyz from the current joints (IK only; nothing moves). status unreachable means move_to would refuse it; unknown means the check could not run.
doc.code:
IK reach check from the current joints, nothing moves (--ik): {status: reachable | unreachable | unknown, q, position_err, orientation_err, message}.

Example:
    if preview_reach([0.05, 0.12, 0.95])["status"] != "unreachable":
        move_to([0.05, 0.12, 0.95])

gripper.description: -1 open (default), +1 close; a program may pass None to keep the last command

doc.tool: Scripted EEF servo to a world xyz; holds orientation. gripper -1 = open, +1 = close (hold +1 while carrying). Never move more than 0.30 m in xy in one call; split long moves.
doc.code:
Servo the end effector to a world xyz, holding its orientation (or turning to target_yaw). gripper -1 opens (the default), +1 closes: pass gripper=1 on every move while carrying. Refused (ValueError, unmoved) beyond 0.30 m in xy: split long moves into waypoints at carry height; with --ik also when unreachable or no collision-free path exists.

Returns:
    dict with eef_pos, final_dist_m (large: the reach stalled), steps_used, gripper_width, terminated, truncated; planned / stopped with --ik.

Example:
    move_to([0.05, 0.12, 1.05])                 # above the target, open
    move_to([0.05, 0.12, 0.93])
    set_gripper(1, steps=15)
    r = move_to([0.05, 0.12, 1.05], gripper=1)  # carry: keep it closed
    print(r["final_dist_m"])

doc.tool: Servo xyz and pitch/yaw together each step. Use when move_to stalls on deep or low reaches (cabinet fronts, microwave). gripper defaults to -1 (open): pass +1 while holding.
doc.code:
Servo xyz and the pitch / yaw targets (world frame; pitch 0 = pointing down) together each step: the reach that move_to stalls on (cabinet fronts, microwave). gripper defaults to -1 (open): pass 1 while holding.

Returns:
    dict with eef_pos, final_dist_m, final_pitch, steps_used, gripper_width, terminated.

Example:
    r = move_pose([0.1, 0.2, 0.95], target_pitch=0.5, gripper=1)
    print(r["final_dist_m"], r["final_pitch"])

gripper.description: -1 open, +1 close (default); a program may pass None to keep the last command

doc.tool: Rotate the wrist about world z. Give target_yaw (absolute) or delta_yaw (relative), radians. Holds xyz.
doc.code:
Turn the gripper about world z to target_yaw or by delta_yaw (rad, positive = counter-clockwise seen from above), holding its position. gripper defaults to +1 (closed): pass -1 before a grasp.

Returns:
    dict with start_yaw, target_yaw, final_yaw, yaw, final_err, steps_used, eef_pos.

Example:
    r = rotate_wrist(delta_yaw=1.5708, gripper=-1)   # a quarter turn, open
    print(r["final_yaw"], r["final_err"])

gripper.description: -1 open, +1 close (default); a program may pass None to keep the last command

doc.tool: Tilt the gripper about world x (pitch 0 = pointing down, +pi/2 = pointing +y). Give target_pitch or delta_pitch, radians. Holds xyz and yaw. Use before entering a narrow opening facing ±y.
doc.code:
Tilt the gripper about world x (pitch 0 = pointing down, +pi/2 = pointing +y) to target_pitch or by delta_pitch (rad), holding its position and yaw. gripper defaults to +1 (closed).

Returns:
    dict with start_pitch, target_pitch, final_pitch, final_err, steps_used, eef_pos.

Example:
    rotate_pitch(target_pitch=0.6)
    move_to([0.0, 0.25, 1.0], gripper=1)

gripper.description: -1 opens, +1 closes; omitted keeps the last command

doc.code:
Move the end effector by a world-frame offset (+x away from the robot toward the agentview camera, +y robot-left, +z up), holding its orientation; at most 0.10 m per call. moved_m well below the command: blocked by contact, the table or a limit.

Returns:
    dict with eef_pos, moved_m, steps_used, gripper_width, terminated.

Example:
    r = move_delta([0, 0, -0.05])   # descend 5 cm
    print(r["moved_m"])

gripper.description: -1 opens, +1 closes; omitted keeps the last command

doc.code:
Turn the gripper about world z by delta_yaw radians (positive = counter-clockwise seen from above; at most pi/2 per call), holding its position and the gripper command.

Returns:
    dict with yaw, final_err, steps_used, eef_pos.

Example:
    r = rotate_delta(0.5)
    print(r["yaw"], r["final_err"])

gripper.description: -1 open (default), +1 close; a program may pass None to keep the last command

doc.tool: Hold the pose and drive the gripper for `steps` env steps (e.g. +1 for 8-12 steps to firm a grip).
doc.code:
Hold the pose and drive the gripper (-1 open, the default; +1 close) for `steps` env steps; the fingers travel about 1 mm per step and stop on a grasped object. Close with about 15 steps; +1 for 8-12 steps firms a grip.

Returns:
    dict with gripper, gripper_width (0.01-0.05 holding, near 0 closed on nothing), steps_used, terminated.

Example:
    set_gripper(1, steps=15)
    if get_state()["gripper_width"] < 0.01:
        print("missed")

doc.tool: Open the gripper in place for up to max_steps; triggers termination when the goal predicate holds.
doc.code:
Open the gripper in place for max_steps env steps; placing may end the task (terminated).

Returns:
    dict with start_gripper_opening, final_gripper_opening, steps_used, terminated.

Example:
    r = release()
    print(r["terminated"], r["final_gripper_opening"])

doc.tool: Pi0.5 closed-loop grasp. Use it only for the grasp; you do every move_to and release. Success needs a descent then a lift with the gripper partly closed; it is a hint, confirm from gripper opening and the wrist image.

OpenVLA (7B, LIBERO fine-tune; one action per call) closed-loop grasp, run as action chunks until the pick heuristics say the object is lifted or the budget ends. Use it only for the grasp; you do every move_to and release. Success needs a descent then a lift with the gripper partly closed; it is a hint, confirm from gripper opening and the wrist image.

OpenVLA-OFT (7B, LIBERO fine-tune; 8-step chunks) closed-loop grasp, run as action chunks until the pick heuristics say the object is lifted or the budget ends. Use it only for the grasp; you do every move_to and release. Success needs a descent then a lift with the gripper partly closed; it is a hint, confirm from gripper opening and the wrist image.

GR00T N1.6/N1.7 (LIBERO libero_panda fine-tune; 16-step chunks) closed-loop grasp, run as action chunks until the pick heuristics say the object is lifted or the budget ends. Use it only for the grasp; you do every move_to and release. Success needs a descent then a lift with the gripper partly closed; it is a hint, confirm from gripper opening and the wrist image.
Pi0.5 closed-loop contact skill for non-pick interactions (knob, stove, drawer, button, short push). success only mirrors task termination; inspect the images for intermediate progress.

standoff.description: Pre-grasp distance along the approach, m (default 0.10)

doc.tool: Execute one planned grasp (a g id of the current observation, from plan_grasp) in one call: open to the pre-grasp standoff back along its approach, descend to it with its pitch and yaw, close, lift straight up. Returns each leg's final_dist_m and gripper_width (0.01-0.05 holding, near 0 missed); error and stalled when a leg stopped short. The id is spent either way; afterwards plan_place with this grasp_id plans from the held object.
doc.code:
Execute one planned grasp (a g id of the current observation) from a single resolution of the id: open to the pre-grasp standoff back along its approach, descend to it with its pitch and yaw, close, lift straight up. error and stalled when a leg stopped short (the robot moved: plan again). Afterwards plan_place(region, that grasp id) plans from the held object.

Returns:
    dict with legs, gripper_width (0.01-0.05 holding, near 0 missed), eef_pos, terminated; error / stalled.

Example:
    g = plan_grasp("black bowl")
    r = execute_grasp(g["active"])
    print(r["gripper_width"])

standoff.description: Pre-place distance along the approach, m (default 0.10)

doc.tool: Execute one planned place (a p id of the current observation, from plan_place) in one call: carry closed to the pre-place standoff, descend to the place pose, open, retreat to the pre-place. Returns each leg's final_dist_m; error and stalled when a leg stopped short.
doc.code:
Execute one planned place (a p id of the current observation) from a single resolution of the id: carry closed to the pre-place standoff, descend to the place pose, open, retreat.

Returns:
    dict with legs, gripper_width, eef_pos, terminated (placing may finish the task); error / stalled.

Example:
    p = plan_place("plate", g["active"])
    r = execute_place(p["active"])
    print(r["terminated"])

Camera intrinsics and extrinsics of a LIBERO camera at a resolution (images rendered by render_camera are upside down).

Example:
    meta = get_camera_meta("agentview", 512, 512)
    K = meta["intrinsic_K"]

One LIBERO camera's raw RGB frame (and normalized depth buffer), upside down as MuJoCo renders it.

Example:
    rgb, depth = render_camera("agentview", 256, 256, depth=True)

The simulator's current observation: the robot's own robot0_* keys and the images (object poses are privileged).

Example:
    o = raw_obs()
    print(o["robot0_eef_pos"], o["robot0_gripper_qpos"])

One OSC action [dx, dy, dz, drx, dry, drz, gripper] in [-1, 1] (0.05 m and 0.1 rad per unit; gripper -1 open, +1 close).

Example:
    step([0, 0, 0.5, 0, 0, 0, -1])   # up 2.5 cm, open

Run a chunk of OSC actions [N, 7] in one call.

Example:
    chunk_step([[0, 0, 0.5, 0, 0, 0, -1]] * 4)

object_name.description: The object in words, e.g. 'black bowl'

use_multiview.description: Also segment in the wrist view (default true)

doc.tool: Pose of an object named in words, from SAM3 masks and depth (agentview and wrist): [position (3,), quaternion_wxyz (4,)], or [null, null]. The quaternion may be unreliable: for placing use the grasp quaternion or [0, 1, 0, 0] (gripper down).
doc.code:
Get the pose of an object from a natural language description (SAM3 + depth).
The quaternion may be unreliable: disregard it and use the grasp quaternion or [0, 1, 0, 0] (wxyz, gripper down) for placement. It may return (None, None).

Args:
    object_name: the object, e.g. "black bowl".
    use_multiview: also use the wrist camera (default True).

Returns:
    [position (3,), quaternion_wxyz (4,)] in the world frame.

Example:
    pos, quat = get_object_pose("woven basket")

doc.tool: Privileged: the simulator's pose of an object named in words: [position (3,), quaternion_wxyz (4,)].
doc.code:
Get the pose of an object from the simulator (privileged): "<name>_1", else the one object whose name contains the words.

Returns:
    [position (3,), quaternion_wxyz (4,)].

Example:
    pos, quat = get_object_pose("basket")

use_multiview.description: Also segment in the wrist view (default true)

doc.tool: A grasp of an object named in words: [position (3,), quaternion_wxyz (4,)] for goto_pose. With a grasp server the best planned grasp, else top-down over the object's centre, 3 cm below its top.
doc.code:
Sample a grasp pose for an object from a natural language description. Use its quaternion.

Returns:
    [position (3,), quaternion_wxyz (4,)].

Example:
    pos, quat = sample_grasp_pose("milk carton")
    goto_pose(pos, quat, z_approach=0.1)

doc.tool: Privileged: a grasp of an object named in words, from the simulator: its position with the gripper pointing down.
doc.code:
Sample a grasp pose for an object (privileged: the simulator's position, gripper down [0, 1, 0, 0]).

Example:
    pos, quat = sample_grasp_pose("milk")

position.description: World [x, y, z] of the grip point, m

z_approach.description: First stop this far back along the approach axis, m (default 0)

doc.tool: Go to a gripper pose (position and wxyz orientation), keeping the gripper command; with z_approach first stop that far back along the approach axis. The gripper stays pointing down and turns to the pose's yaw; long moves run as straight legs.
doc.code:
Go to pose. There is no need to call a second goto_pose with the same pose after calling it with z_approach. The gripper points down and turns to the quaternion's yaw (tilt_rad in the result: the tilt not reached).

Args:
    position: (3,) XYZ in meters.
    quaternion_wxyz: (4,) WXYZ unit quaternion.
    z_approach: first arrive z_approach metres back along the gripper's approach axis.

Example:
    goto_pose(pos, quat, z_approach=0.1)

doc.tool: Move the gripper back to its position and yaw at the episode's start.
doc.code:
Move the robot to a safe home pose (the gripper's pose at the episode's start).

Example:
    home_pose()

doc.tool: Open the gripper fully (40 env steps).
doc.code:
Open gripper fully.

Example:
    open_gripper()

doc.tool: Close the gripper fully (60 env steps; the fingers stop on an object).
doc.code:
Close gripper fully.

Example:
    close_gripper()

doc.tool: Predict grasps for one object from the current RGB-D observation, ranked best first, in the world frame. Give the object as text (segmented with SAM3) or a mask_id of this observation. Each candidate has a short id (g3) and its EEF pose, valid until the robot moves or the scene changes; execute_grasp runs one from a single resolution of its id. Try `active` first; when it is refused before the robot moves (unreachable), call again with next_after=<that id> to get the next rank without re-planning; after a failed motion, plan again.
doc.code:
Grasp candidates for one object of the current observation, world frame, best first; ids (g3) expire when the robot moves. next_after=<id> rejects a candidate and returns the next rank.

Example:
    g = plan_grasp("red cube")
    best = g["candidates"][0]
    print(best["id"], best["eef_position"])

doc.tool: Where to hold the grasped object so it comes to rest on a placement region (AnyPlace). Give the region as text (segmented now) or as a mask id, and the grasp id: after execute_grasp, that grasp's id (the held object is found again from its prompt as the mask nearest the gripper, or object_mask_id, and the gripper's actual pose is used; refused when the fingers hold nothing); before it, a current g id with region and object from the same observation. Returns place poses with ids (p1); execute_place runs one.
doc.code:
AnyPlace: place poses (p ids) for the held object on a region. Before the grasp: region mask and grasp from one observation; after executing it: the executed grasp's id, the region from the current observation.

Example:
    p = plan_place("green plate", g["candidates"][0]["id"])

waypoints.description: World-frame [x, y, z] positions in m, in order

gripper.description: Gripper command held along the route: -1 open, +1 closed (+1 while carrying). Required: the route never changes the gripper by default

doc.tool: Move the EEF through 1-5 world-frame positions in order (orientation and gripper held). Checked before anything moves: each segment and the whole route against the per-call limits, each waypoint against the workspace. Stops at the first waypoint not reached. Use it for short routes around an obstacle (lift, carry, descend) instead of one straight move.

point.description: Target pixel [row, col] in the wrist image

row.description: target pixel row in the wrist image

execute.description: Also move by the correction (default false)

doc.tool: Wrist-view alignment near a grasp: give the target's pixel [row, col] in the current wrist image. Returns the lateral EEF correction (in the camera's image plane, at the target's depth, at most max_correction_m) that puts the target under the gripper centre (delta_world) and the EEF position after it (aligned_xyz). execute=true also applies it (the move_to servo to aligned_xyz); by default nothing moves. Approach depth and orientation are unchanged. The returned wrist image marks the gripper-centre pixel (green) and the target (red).
doc.code:
The lateral EEF correction that puts pixel (row, col) of the current 512x512 wrist image under the gripper centre (in the camera's image plane, at the target's depth, at most max_correction_m): desired_pixel, target_pixel, delta_world, aligned_xyz. execute=True also moves by it (env.move_to to aligned_xyz).

Example:
    a = align_wrist(250, 270)
    align_wrist(250, 270, execute=True)

object.description: Without a grasp backend: the object to grasp, e.g. 'black bowl' (required then)

max_candidates.description: With a grasp backend: how many plan_grasp candidates to show (default 8)

doc.tool: A separate vision model's grasp opinion (--grasp-advisor), never moving the robot. With a grasp backend: it sees the latest plan_grasp candidates drawn on the camera image (jaw line, centre dot, approach arrow, one colour each) and recommends the one most likely to hold through lift and carry, or abstains; run the recommended id with execute_grasp (or pass it as grasp_id); call it right after plan_grasp, before the robot moves. Without one: give `object`; it proposes the grasp centre, jaw contacts and top/side approach on the camera image, back-projected to a world grasp (position, approach, eef_yaw, pregrasp_xyz), marked confidence_level low (one image, no width or collision check): approach through pregrasp_xyz and confirm in the wrist view.
